about: An invented story for tuning the consistency questions, the fix and State Upkeep. Each case is one reply with what it follows from; base holds what a case leaves out. slips names the questions that should flag it; gone holds words the fix must remove, kept words that must survive. upkeep.has and upkeep.not name State Upkeep operations as op:slot or op:name.

base.pcLooks: Lean, sun-browned woman in her thirties, short black hair, a pale scar through her left eyebrow, grey eyes.
carrying: wool cloak, rolled and tied behind her saddle
base.location: Caravan camp at the Well of Ashar

cast.name: Tamsin
cast.appearance: Stocky woman in her sixties, white hair in a single long braid, deeply weathered face, missing the two smallest fingers of her right hand, indigo head-wrap, long leather vest over a faded red robe.

cast.name: Jory
cast.appearance: Gangly boy of about fourteen, red curly hair, freckles, a too-large green tunic belted with rope, barefoot.

cast.name: Captain Vane
cast.appearance: Tall man in his forties, shaved head, close-trimmed black beard, a burn scar down the left side of his neck, dusty blue officer's coat with brass buttons, a sabre at his hip.

facts: Tamsin's son Pell drowned in the spring flood two years ago.
Captain Vane confiscated Wren's pistol at the border post.
The letter for the Governor must not be opened.
base.summary: Wren joined Tamsin's salt caravan at Port Lell to carry sealed letters inland. At the border post Captain Vane searched the wagons, confiscated Wren's pistol and chose to ride along. On the first night someone cut a waterskin; Tamsin blamed the heat, Wren suspects Vane. Today they reached the Well of Ashar.
memories: 8th of Dry Month, dawn: Wren found a waterskin slit open beside the third camel. Jory swore he had been asleep. Vane said nothing and watched Tamsin.
8th of Dry Month, noon: a sandstorm drove the caravan behind the Red Teeth rocks. Vane's horse bolted into the storm and was lost; he now rides the spare camel, Bitter.
9th of Dry Month, morning: Tamsin told Wren privately that the Governor owes her money. Jory found a brass button in the sand where the cut waterskin had lain and gave it to Wren.
base.previous:
The sun hung low and orange over the dunes as the caravan settled around the Well of Ashar. Three tents went up in a crooked row. Tamsin limped along the line of camels, slapping flanks and counting under her breath, while Jory hauled the well's rope hand over hand, his oversized tunic dark with sweat. Captain Vane sat apart on Bitter's saddle, laid on the sand, cleaning his sabre with slow strokes of an oiled rag. He did not look up when Wren passed, though the blade caught the light each time he turned it.

Tamsin spat. “Water tonight, at least,” she said. “Tomorrow the Glass Flats.”

Wren felt the brass button in her pocket, still warm from Jory's hand.
base.input: I walk over to Vane and show him the brass button.
base.reply:
Vane's rag stopped mid-stroke when Wren held out the button. He looked at it for a long moment, then at the row of brass buttons down his own blue coat, every one in its place.

“Half the officers on this road wear those,” he said. “They sell them by the gross in Port Lell.”

“Jory found it where the waterskin was cut.”

“Then someone dropped it there.” He went back to the sabre. “Ask the boy where he really was that night, courier. Boys lie.”

Across the camp, Tamsin had stopped counting camels and was watching them, her indigo head-wrap pulled low against the slanting light.
